text.p: Shares in HSBC Holdings Plc fell on Monday despite gains in the Hang Seng index earlier today, amid profit-taking and following downgrades on the stock last week due to the strength of sterling, traders said.
HSBC shares, which set an intraday record of 13.16 stg on November 6, were down 14p at 12.65 stg in moderate trading of 1.2 million shares.
Earlier the Hang Seng in Hong Kong, where half HSBC's shares are owned, was up 153.43 points or 1.2 percent.
Last week analysts at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett said they were considering trimming earnings estimates to reflect sterling strength.
"We saw some big profit downgrades last week and it was all because of the currency angle," said the head of equity trading at one leading brokerage.
Others said there were signs that some investors were cashing in their gains on the stock.
"There seems to have been some resistance around the 13.00 stg level," said one market marker, "we have seen a bit of top slicing and there has been a decent seller around."
"It has been a good performer and people may be switching into other banks. There just seems to have been some stock available in HSBC at this level."
Elsewhere in the bank sector Barclays was up 2p at 964, NatWest was up 2-1/2p at 692-1/2 and Standard Chartered was up 4-1/2p at 663.
